_about: AI governance policy for Chatbot Compare. Changing this file changes its version hash, which every run, gate result and sign-off records. Bump 'version' whenever a threshold changes. See README 'AI governance'.

voltkart.name: VoltKart support bot
voltkart.intended_use: Answer VoltKart customers' questions about products, prices, stock, orders and store policies from the store's own data, and hand anything else to a human.
voltkart.users: Retail customers in India, in English, Hindi and Hinglish.
voltkart.out_of_scope: Medical, legal, financial or investment advice; payments; changing orders without verification; anything about other customers.
voltkart.eu_ai_act: Limited risk: a customer-facing chatbot, so Art. 50(1) applies (customers must be told they are talking to an AI).

hussain.name: Reliance Digital multi-agent bot
hussain.intended_use: Sales, order, service-ticket and product questions for an electronics store, routed to a sales, service (ResQ) or RAG agent.
hussain.out_of_scope: Medical, legal, financial or investment advice; payments; anything about other customers.
hussain.eu_ai_act: Limited risk: a customer-facing chatbot, so Art. 50(1) applies (customers must be told they are talking to an AI).

mouni.name: SupportFlow AI
mouni.intended_use: Customer support for orders and products, with intent detection and handoff to a human agent.
mouni.out_of_scope: Medical, legal, financial or investment advice; payments; anything about other customers.
mouni.eu_ai_act: Limited risk: a customer-facing chatbot, so Art. 50(1) applies (customers must be told they are talking to an AI).

release_gate._about: A bot can be signed off for release from a run only if every 'block' rule passes. 'warn' rules are shown but don't block. Failures counted per case: a case fails if any of its scored samples (repeats, rewordings) failed.

models._about: The model inventory: what may be used, as glob patterns. Bot LLMs match bots.json 'llm'; judges match the model that gave each verdict. Paid models need the owner's approval (see 'approved_paid').

approved_paid.Claude *: Amazon Bedrock, billed to the project AWS account; approved by the owner on 2026-10-07 for the VoltKart chatbot only, not for judging.

data._about: pii: 'redact' masks personal data that appears only in bot replies before a conversation is sent to a judge that isn't on this machine; 'flag' sends it but records it; 'off' does neither. Test data in suites and store data files must be synthetic.

risks.title: Prompt injection makes the bot ignore its instructions or reveal hidden data
frameworks: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.7 (security and resilience)
risks.mitigation: Direct, multi-turn, encoded, Hinglish and fake-authority injection cases plus reworded variants; critical regression alert when one breaks.

risks.title: The bot discloses another customer's personal data, card numbers or OTPs
risks.mitigation: Guardrail cases with zero tolerance in the release gate; white-box check that no private-data tool is called on an injection.

risks.title: The bot invents prices, specs, policies or delivery details
frameworks: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.5 (valid and reliable)
risks.mitigation: Hallucination cases, judge flags any invented fact in every case, grounded check against what the bot retrieved.

risks.title: Customers are treated differently by gender, religion, caste, region, age, disability or language
frameworks: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.11 (fairness and bias)
risks.mitigation: Paired-persona bias cases judged side by side, reworded variants, critical regression alert.

risks.title: The bot gives medical, legal, financial or other advice outside its purpose
risks.mitigation: Out-of-scope cases; intended use and out-of-scope uses recorded per system in governance.json.

risks.title: Customers get wrong answers about products and orders
frameworks: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.5 (valid and reliable)
risks.mitigation: Factual cases with exact checks and an AI judge; bootstrapped ranges and repeats.

risks.title: The AI judge grades wrongly, so scores and release decisions are wrong
risks.mitigation: Second judge from another model family; human review queue with random spot-checks and Wilson intervals.

risks.title: A change to a bot silently breaks safety, accuracy or fairness
risks.mitigation: Baselines, nightly regression run with exit codes and webhook, release gate blocks on critical regressions.

risks.title: Personal data in conversations is sent to a third-party free-tier judge that may train on it
risks.mitigation: Synthetic test data only; unknown personal data in bot replies is masked before any cloud judge call and counted on the result; retention limit on saved runs.

risks.title: An unapproved or paid model is used without the owner's approval
frameworks: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.6 (AI system inventory)
risks.mitigation: Model inventory in governance.json; the release gate blocks runs with a bot LLM or judge outside it.

risks.title: Customers aren't told they are talking to an AI
frameworks: EU AI Act Art. 50(1) (transparency for AI that interacts with people)
risks.mitigation: Manual check of each bot's greeting and UI before release; record it in the sign-off note.

risks.title: A result can't be traced to the code, suite, bots and judge that produced it, or is edited afterwards
frameworks: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.4 (documented risk management)
risks.mitigation: Provenance on every run; hash-chained audit log; each finished run sealed with the hash of its results.
